about: The first of three prayers said secretly by the priest before Communion. Its opening quotes John 14:27. The priest asks Christ to regard not his sins but the faith of the Church, and to grant the Church peace and unity.

s01.narrative: The priest bows over the altar with his hands joined upon it, and says the three prayers that follow secretly.

s02.translation: Lord Jesus Christ, who said to Your Apostles:

s03.translation: Peace I leave you, My peace I give you:

s04.translation: look not on our sins, but on the faith of Your Church;

s05.translation: and graciously grant her peace and unity in accordance with Your will:

s06.translation: Who live and reign for ever and ever. Amen.

s07.narrative: In Masses for the dead the peace is not given, and this prayer is left out.

w009.function: Relínquo is what a man does with what he leaves behind at his going. The words were spoken on the eve of the Passion.

w012.function: The second time the word is said it is qualified: not peace of any kind, but His own — and the quotation stops just before the Gospel's not as the world gives.

w015.function: With the subjunctive “respícias” (w016) it makes a negative petition, as it does in the Lord's Prayer: do not look.

w016.function: Re- and spício: to look back at, to turn and take notice. The prayer asks Him to turn His face one way and not the other.

w018.function: “My” — and the owner is the priest alone, though he is about to ask for the whole Church: the sins are his own, the faith is not. The form is accusative plural, with “peccáta” (w017).

w020.function: Set against “peccáta” (w017) as the thing to be looked at instead. The two accusatives are the two objects offered to the same verb.

w023.function: Two feminine nouns stand within reach — the faith and the Church — and the form settles neither. The two things asked, peace and gathering into one, are asked for the Church, and that is how the prayer is read.

w027.function: One of two infinitives depending on “dignéris” (w030). A verb made from pax, to make peaceful.

w029.function: Co- and adunáre, to bring to one: not to reconcile parties but to make many into one thing.

w030.function: The courtly construction of the Roman prayers: not “do this” but “think it worthy to do this” — hence the two infinitives that complete it.

w035.function: Nominative standing with the two verbs, not an address: who as God livest and reignest.
